solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Practitioner of magic gets response in Arab country

indicators.note: in places the preceding piece inside the country that follows

blocks.note: the sultanate on the Arabian peninsula
the two letters the grid needs from this word; the setter's sense here is unclear

explanation.surface: A conjuror wins a warm reception while performing in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: O(BI)MAN: OMAN wraps BI. How 'response' yields BI is not clear from any standard sense, so this piece is uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: An obeah man is a West Indian sorcerer, someone who works obi or obeah witchcraft.

clue.text: Not apt to work? One makes a choice

indicators.note: putting letters to work sets them in motion into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone unsuited to their job turns out to be good at deciding.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark lets the opening half double as a hint: an optant is anything but unfit to choose.
explanation.definitionFit: An optant is a person who exercises an option, especially in choosing a nationality.

clue.text: Couple having sex upset this writer

indicators.note: in a down entry something upset is turned upside down, so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: IT is slang for sex appeal or sex
the setter refers to themself

explanation.surface: A pair's love life has thrown the author into a state.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a couple in a romantic relationship, as in 'they're an item'.

clue.text: Writer's transgression — gosh, is policeman brought in?!

indicators.note: what is brought in ends up enclosed by the surrounding exclamation

blocks.note: 'My!' is an exclamation of surprise
taken as written
slang for a police officer

explanation.surface: An author caught out in some offence exclaims that the police are being called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gosh' is the surrounding exclamation, and 'brought in' puts the next two words inside it; the ?! marks the mock outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: To miscopy is to make an error in transcribing, a slip a writer or scribe commits.

clue.text: Strange pal I only start to understand at most

indicators.note: something strange is out of its usual form, so the letters are rearranged
only the start of the following word is wanted

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of understand

explanation.surface: An odd friend can grasp only so much at best.
explanation.definitionFit: Al più is an Italian musical direction meaning at the most.

clue.text: Guess about winter month becoming fresher

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first piece surrounds the month

blocks.note: a bet is a guess, as in 'my bet is'
short form of January

explanation.surface: Someone speculates about which cold month turns things new.
explanation.walkthrough: BE(JAN)T. Fresher is the British word for a first-year university student.
explanation.definitionFit: A bejant is a first-year student at a Scottish university such as St Andrews.

clue.text: The fellow joining graduate society, a group once in parliament

blocks.note: Bachelor of Arts
abbreviation for society
the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man signing up to a graduates' club that used to sit in the legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: Parliament here is the old French parlement, a law court, not a legislature.
explanation.definitionFit: The basoche was the guild of law clerks attached to the Paris parlement before the Revolution.

clue.text: Reversal of bent pipe requires rare hard graft

indicators.note: reversal says outright that the following word reads backwards

blocks.note: a crane is a bent pipe or siphon for drawing liquid
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
no letters: flags the definition as a rare usage

explanation.surface: Fixing a kinked pipe backwards takes unusually tough work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rare' marks the definition as an uncommon usage. 'Hard graft' looks like a phrase meaning toil; it splits into H and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To enarch is a rare variant of inarch, to graft a plant by joining it to another still on its own roots.

clue.text: Plant discovering metallic element in sulphate

indicators.note: in puts the metallic element inside the sulphate

blocks.note: alum is a double sulphate of aluminium and potassium
Li is the symbol for lithium

explanation.surface: A plant is found to contain some metal in its sulphate.
explanation.walkthrough: AL(LI)UM.
explanation.definitionFit: Allium is the plant genus including onion, garlic and leek.

clue.text: Lined metal, face of it having been scratched, could be this

definitions.text: Lined metal, face of it having been scratched, could be this

indicators.text: face of it having been scratched
indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, and scratching it off removes the first letter
could be suggests the letters might be rearranged into something else

blocks.note: taken as written
the word without its opening letter

explanation.surface: Engraved metal, its surface scored, might be described by this word.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: niello work fills engraved lines in metal, so scratched lined metal is exactly what is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Niellated means decorated with niello, a black metallic alloy inlaid into lines engraved on metal.

clue.text: Cheryl, resembling a well-off country girl?

blocks.note: first meaning: the surname of the singer Cheryl, born Cheryl ..., of Girls Aloud
second meaning: like a prosperous rural type in tweeds

explanation.walkthrough: Cheryl Tweedy is the birth name of the British pop singer known as Cheryl; the question mark flags the loose second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweedy describes the dress and manner of the country gentry, who favour tweed clothing.

clue.text: Favourite worker keeping not very well? Only sparkling a bit

indicators.note: the outer pieces keep the next word held inside them

blocks.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
unwell
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A favourite employee who is under the weather is only slightly lively.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that ill is more than just 'not very well'. The definition describes wine, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Pétillant is the wine term for lightly sparkling, less fizzy than fully sparkling wine.

clue.text: Actors in the places such as Bath not active

indicators.note: not tells us to drop the letter standing for active

blocks.note: Bath is a famous English spa town
A is the abbreviation for active

explanation.surface: Players performing in English spa towns, though resting.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SPAS loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Thesps is informal for thespians, i.e. actors, after Thespis, the legendary first Greek actor.

clue.text: Line in insect — colour gone

indicators.note: in places the line inside the insect

blocks.note: the honey-making insect
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A striped insect has lost its colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: B(L)EE. 'gone' marks the word as obsolete; it means colour or complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: Blee is an archaic word for colour or complexion, surviving in Scots.

clue.text: Pure model done out as a swimmer in the sea

indicators.note: a room done out is redecorated, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A flawless fashion model dresses up as a mermaid or other sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Loup de mer, French for sea wolf, is the European sea bass, a fish of the open sea.

clue.text: Twisted priest to run around

indicators.note: turning around means the pieces are read backwards

blocks.note: Eli, the priest who brought up Samuel in the Bible
to trot is to run at a gentle pace

explanation.surface: A distorted clergyman sets off on a jog.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI + TROT, all reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortile means twisted or coiled, from the same root as tortuous.

clue.text: Troublesome old boy about to grab second person

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the boy is read backwards
grabbing takes something into a grip, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: a male child
the second-person pronoun

explanation.surface: An awkward old boy is about to collar the next person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old boy' looks like OB, but 'old' is part of the definition, flagging an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Noyous is an obsolete word for annoying or harmful, from the same root as noisome and annoy.

clue.text: Old head covering needed by daughter? Fiona's not warm

blocks.note: a caul was a close-fitting cap or net worn by women
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter needing an old-fashioned bonnet because a woman is chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiona is a typically Scottish name, signalling a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cauld is the Scots form of cold, the opposite of warm as a Scot like Fiona would say it.

clue.text: Put earth around a withering plant

indicators.note: withering away means the article named disappears from the soil it sits in
moving letters around rearranges them into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the word with its A dropped

explanation.surface: A gardener mounds soil around a plant that is drooping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is the letter that withers from earth; the rest of PUT and EARTH is jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpeth is an East Indian climbing plant of the bindweed family whose root was used as a purgative.

clue.text: With drug comes hallucinatory experience (taste not good)

indicators.note: not good asks us to drop the letter standing for good

blocks.note: a trip is a drug-induced hallucinatory episode
a tang is a sharp taste
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Taking a drug brings on a bad trip with an unpleasant taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A triptan is any of a class of drugs such as sumatriptan used to treat migraine.

clue.text: Exceptionally fit maid, one in an Islamic dynasty?

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters leave their usual order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An unusually athletic servant belongs to a Muslim ruling house.
explanation.definitionFit: A Fatimid is a member of the dynasty claiming descent from Fatima that ruled North Africa and Egypt 909 to 1171.

clue.text: One goat with another almost falling in sunken wood

indicators.note: almost means falling just short, so the last letter goes
falling in puts that piece inside the first goat

blocks.note: bok is a South African word for a goat
another goat, the second one in the clue

explanation.surface: Two goats, one nearly tumbling into a sunken wood.
explanation.walkthrough: Bok, a South African goat, is a crossword favourite; the second goat is unnamed, just 'another'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bog oak is ancient oak preserved black in peat bogs, wood that has lain sunk in a bog.

clue.text: Nitrogen trichloride's turned up in American plant

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: agene is nitrogen trichloride, once used to bleach flour; with the 's

explanation.surface: A toxic chemical surfaces in an American plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Senega is a North American milkwort whose root, snakeroot, was used medicinally.

clue.text: What physicist here could produce weather map?

blocks.clueFragment: What physicist here could produce weather map?
blocks.note: surface reading: which scientist on this spot could draw up a forecast chart
setter's reading: the letters of 'What' plus those of the physicist in this entry, shuffled, make up WEATHER MAP

explanation.surface: Asking which scientist present could draw up a forecast chart.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer's letters with W, H, A, T rearrange to WEATHER MAP, so 'here' points to the entry itself.
explanation.definitionFit: André-Marie Ampère was the French physicist who founded electrodynamics; the unit of current bears his name.

clue.text: Repudiates Fleet Street etc in declamations

indicators.note: in puts the street's area inside the declamations

blocks.note: rants are loud declamatory speeches
EC is the City of London postal district that includes Fleet Street

explanation.surface: The press take back what they said in their tirades.
explanation.walkthrough: R(EC)ANTS. Fleet Street, the old home of London's newspapers, lies in the EC postcode area.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to withdraw a former statement or belief, i.e. to repudiate it.

clue.text: Keep quiet about solicitor's past crime in Glasgow?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the call for quiet wraps the next piece

blocks.note: 'Sh!' asks for silence
a tout solicits custom

explanation.surface: Hushing up a lawyer's history of offences north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: S(TOUT)H. Solicitor suggests a British lawyer but means someone soliciting; Glasgow signals a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stouth is an old Scots word for theft, a crime of the past in Scotland.

clue.text: Theatre getting reproach in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: odium is disgrace or reproach

explanation.surface: A playhouse draws criticism from the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The auditorium is both a part of the theatre and the place sound is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: An odeum is an ancient Greek or Roman building for musical performances, i.e. a theatre.

clue.text: Basher of duds in conflict — time to move on

indicators.note: moving on takes the letter out of its place so it can go further along

blocks.note: a battle is armed conflict
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A thug who beats up failures in a war is told it is time to go.
explanation.walkthrough: One T of BATTLE moves to the end. Duds is slang for clothes, not failures.
explanation.definitionFit: A batlet is a small wooden bat once used to beat clothes being washed.

clue.text: Skunk beginning to eat bit of worm

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the atok is a South American skunk
the opening letter of eat

explanation.surface: A skunk starts to eat part of a worm.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoke is the asexual front portion of certain marine bristle worms, as opposed to the reproductive epitoke.

clue.text: Yarn written with pen, page being out of order

indicators.note: things out of order are not in their proper sequence, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A story set down with a pen whose pages are jumbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' suggests a story, but here it is literal thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Genappe is a smooth worsted yarn used in braids and fringes, named after the Belgian town.

clue.text: Looking angry about duck having tiny eggs

indicators.note: about means around, so the colour surrounds the duck

blocks.note: red in the face with anger
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A cross-looking figure stands over a duck with small eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: R(O)ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Roed means containing roe, the mass of tiny fish eggs.

clue.text: Measure coming with Home Rule

indicators.note: what comes with the following words is carried inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A political step arrives alongside Irish self-government.
explanation.walkthrough: Home Rule was the campaign for Irish self-government within the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: An omer is an ancient Hebrew dry measure, a tenth of an ephah.

clue.text: Game with fiddle — all right after order is introduced

indicators.note: introduced means brought inside, so these pieces go into the fiddle

blocks.note: a gu is a Shetland fiddle
the Order of Merit
okay

explanation.surface: A game involving cheating, deemed fine once rules are brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like cheating but is the Shetland violin; 'order' is the British honour, the Order of Merit.
explanation.definitionFit: Gomoku is a Japanese board game in which players try to get five stones in a row.

clue.text: Most bad-tempered row that is on street after start of curfew

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of curfew
a rank is a row, as of soldiers or taxis
i.e., id est
abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: The grumpiest argument breaks out in the street once curfew begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as a quarrel; it is a line. 'on' and 'after' fix the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranky means irritable, so the crankiest is the most irritable.

clue.text: King, dissolute fellow, bit of nasty monster

indicators.note: only a small bit, the opening letter, of the word is used

blocks.note: K for king in chess
a rake is a dissolute man
the opening letter of nasty

explanation.surface: A debauched king, something of a nasty brute.
explanation.definitionFit: The kraken is a legendary giant sea monster of Norwegian folklore.

clue.text: Enclosure had to be put back after appearance of harmful fly

indicators.note: put back means returned the way it came, so read backwards

blocks.note: a ked is a wingless fly that parasitises sheep
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pen had to be moved after a nasty fly showed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after appearance of' puts the reversed word after KED.
explanation.definitionFit: A keddah is a stockade used in India for trapping wild elephants.
